label: Body-level enforcement for a changelog entry is exactly two warning regexes (CHANGELOG_INTERNAL_ID for [A-Z]{2,4}-\d{3} or T\d{3}, CHANGELOG_TEST_COUNT for digit plus cases/tests/PASS lines) after five blocking frontmatter rules; the spec-folder blockquote and fenced spans are exempt.

The changelog type declares h2DividerRequired true and sectionReferenceChecks false, but the divider check only reads numbered ALL-CAPS H2s and the render checks early-return, so no structural or section rule fires on an unnumbered title-case changelog H2; requiredSections is empty and its finder regex also requires numbering.

No length rule exists anywhere in the validator or the rules file (zero hits for maxLines|max_length|ceiling|maxWords), so the entire concise-format length contract has to be authored rather than relocated.

hvr_scan.py is not in the changelog path: it lives only under sk-create-with-human-voice/scripts, parses hvr-rules.md at run time, covers punctuation and term lists only, and is invoked nowhere in the changelog skill, the command YAMLs or validate_document.py, so Q4 has nothing to extend there.

Measured baselines: short entry 197 lines / 22 H4 / max 5 H4 per section / max 80 H4 body words / no (Level N); long entry 339 lines / 38 H4 / max 7 per section / max 148 words / (Level N) present; the existing test-count regex hits zero times on either version.

An at-a-glance bullet-to-H4 ratio check discriminates where presence alone does not (both entries carry the section): 8 bullets against 22 H4s passes at the 38-H4 count fails, so the check belongs in a new validate_changelog_shape called beside validate_changelog_omissions.

At-a-glance bullet order is not mechanically checkable today because each bullet's bold lead is prose, not a section name, so the template must tag bullets with their section before any order check can exist.

H4 ceilings are mechanical and discriminating: total 26 and per-section 5 both pass the short entry (22, max 5) and fail the long one (38, max 7); the H4 body word ceiling of 90 passes short (80) and fails long (148) with bullet lists and fences excluded.

Folded small fixes are detectable only heuristically: inside one H2, 5 or more H4s with 3 or more bullet-less short bodies flags as unfolded, which does not trigger on the short entry's 2-H4 Runtimes section and does trigger on the long entry's 7-H4 section; the template must supply a canonical fold heading first.

A (Level N) annotation on the spec-folder line is cheap to check, but the line is currently exempt because every blockquote line is skipped wholesale; the narrow fix is a third regex applied to the blockquote instead of masking it.

Maintainer-only detail is not separable by vocabulary: the kept short entry itself names package_skill.py, skill-advisor.cjs, a token delta of 328,333 to 238,406 and a spelled-out count of render checks, so any lexical ban deletes material the target format retains and the drop rule must stay prose in the template.

A file-total ceiling has no infrastructure and cannot ship as blocking: 240 body lines passes the short entry at 197 and fails the long one at 339, but the canonical exemplar is 535 lines, so the exemplar and a blocking ceiling cannot both be canonical.

The brief's premise that upgrade notes are ordered by section is not literally true of the short entry: its design-fundamentals note maps to Retired Surfaces while the next-but-one maps to Frontend Surface, and the list is monotonic only under an unstated rule attributing a retirement's note to the section naming its replacement; one note has no section at all.
Every proposed changelog check must pass .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md at HEAD and fail git show bc28fcbbba:.skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md; a check that passes both adds nothing.

A blocking total-line ceiling cannot land while .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.0.0.md at 535 lines remains the canonical exemplar, because validate.sh --strict runs over the tree the exemplar lives in.
